title: The cloud of unknowing
hookLine: an old English guide says God can be reached by love, but never by thought

lines: AN UNSIGNED BOOK, WITH A WARNING.
STOP TRYING TO FIGURE GOD OUT.
cards: Stop trying to figure God out. That instruction, more or less, sits at the heart of a small English book whose writer never signed it.
The book opens with a warning: whoever holds it shouldn't pass it around to the merely curious, only to someone who means to give their whole life to the practice it describes.
A few chapters in, comes the instruction that sounds backwards for a book about God. Put your thinking down. Not because thinking is bad, the writer says, but because it can't reach that far.

teach.h: A CLOUD ABOVE, A CLOUD OF FORGETTING BELOW.
teach.b: The book is called The Cloud of Unknowing, and its picture has two layers. Above you, between you and God, hangs a cloud of unknowing: dark, thick, impossible to see through with the mind.
Below you, the writer asks you to lay down a cloud of forgetting, and put under it everything else: plans, worries, even good thoughts about holy things.
In chapter six an imagined student asks the obvious question: so how am I supposed to think about God? The writer's answer, in plain paraphrase: I don't know.
God can be loved, but not thought. By love God can be reached and held; by thought, never. So the job isn't to clear the cloud.

teach.h: A SHARP DART OF LONGING LOVE.
teach.b: It's to keep knocking on it, as the book puts it, with a sharp dart of longing love, and not to walk away whatever happens.

teach.h: ONE WORD, FASTENED TO THE HEART.
teach.b: Take one short word, the writer says, a single syllable is best, like God or love. Fasten it to your heart. When thoughts crowd in, answer every one with that word.

teach.h: MOSES DREW NEAR UNTO THE THICK DARKNESS.
teach.b: The Bible has a picture like it, at the mountain in Exodus: "And the people stood afar off, and Moses drew near unto the thick darkness where God was." Not into light. Into thick darkness.
A mantra, the desert's plain names, the Jesus Prayer, the pilgrim's line: this week kept handing a busy mind something small to hold. This book's word doesn't ride the breath.
It's sent upward, like a knock, whenever a thought gets in the way.

how: Readers of The Cloud of Unknowing sit in silence with one short word, such as God or love, and return to it whenever thoughts arrive; the book is also a source for later Christian practices of silent prayer.

games.q: what does “the cloud of unknowing” mean?
o: a fog of doubt that ends a person's faith for good
the dark between the seeker and God, reached by love
the confusion of a mind that has stopped praying

games.q: the cloud of unknowing: tap the pairs.
p: a sharp dart of longing love
what keeps knocking on the cloud
God or love, fastened to the heart

s: the book teaches that thinking hard enough will clear the cloud
the writer says God can be loved but not thought. the job is to keep knocking with love, not to clear the cloud.
the book suggests a word of one syllable, like God or love
a short word, fastened to the heart, to answer every thought that crowds in.
under the cloud of forgetting go only bad thoughts
everything goes under it, even good thoughts about holy things.

games.q: you're the student in chapter six. you ask the writer how you're supposed to think about God. what's the answer?
o: read more books until the picture is clear.
I don't know: God can be loved, but not thought.
think of God as light, and the cloud will lift.
games.why: the writer admits not knowing. God can be reached and held by love, never by thought. so you keep knocking on the cloud with longing love.

practice: Choose a short word: if you pray, the book suggests God or love; if you don't, love works on its own, or any small word you care about. Don't tie it to the breath; just hold it ready.
When a thought arrives, a plan, a worry, a clever idea about this practice, answer it with the word and let the thought slide under the cloud of forgetting.

wordCard.voice: The cloud of unknowing. The dark the mind can't see through, between the seeker and God, in an old English guide. Its way through is love, aimed like a dart, not thought. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew, from Exodus 20:21: the thick darkness Moses drew near to.

carryVoice: Your line: by love, not thought. A knock on the cloud, not a key to it. Until tomorrow.
